rv.q: Through their scenes together, Chowdhury and Chakraborty arrive at moments of strangeness and beauty, too.
Rheology articulates the existential conflict between parent and child: finite time, infinite love.
Rheology would not exist without that relationship and yet it transmutes those truths into something intensely theatrical.
This is but an opening salvo in a 90-minute show that flows according to its own special rules, impossible to categorize but undeniably theatrical and occasionally even thrilling.
Rheology is a remarkable, experimental memento mori play that can’t be categorized or contained within a science flask.
The result is a sometimes brain-stretching exercise in physics and family.
That’s but a small nitpick of what is an otherwise gloriously fresh evening of theatre, a caring meditation on both mortality and familial love.

cn.t: Critics praise "Rheology" as a bold, intellectually stimulating work that seamlessly blends science and theater. Shayok Misha Chowdhury's inventive writing and direction, alongside his mother Bulbul Chakraborty's compelling performance, create a singular theatrical experience.

vr.q: A beautifully original piece that could have only been made by two people who are remarkably close but very different.
if this subject sounds like something interesting to you, then I definitely recommend you go check this out at Playwrights Horizons, because like everything they do, it is really well done.
